display.name: CasperAgent — Agent & LLM Observability
display.description: Agent-native observability for CasperAgent (Mastra + Fireworks) across all THREE OTLP signals — traces, metrics, AND logs. Every query is scoped to service.name = casper-assistant and deployment.environment.name = $environment, so services and deployments cannot silently contaminate one another. Traces panels filter on mastra.span.type (model_generation / tool_call / retrieval / eval / health_watch) over the gen_ai.* semantic conventions. Metrics panels read the first-class OTel counters/histogram the app exports (gen_ai.client.*). Logs panels (bottom row) read the correlated ERROR log records the app emits at each failure — each stamped with the failing span's traceId+spanId, so a log line deep-links to its trace. COST: both the trace formula and the metric counter (gen_ai.client.operation.cost) price every input token at the plain input rate today, because LLM_PRICE_CACHE_READ_PER_MTOK / LLM_PRICE_CACHE_WRITE_PER_MTOK are not configured — the app falls back to the input price for cached tokens (see pricePerToken in src/mastra/llm-telemetry.ts). Cache-read volume is material (620k tokens over the last 24h), so treat the figure as an UPPER BOUND, not an exact bill; set those two env vars to your provider's cache rates and the metric counter becomes the exact, cache-split number. Trace aggregations additionally use casper.self_instrumented = true where appropriate to drop the duplicate span the Mastra native exporter emits for every LLM/tool call.

display.name: Environment
display.description: Value of deployment.environment.name used to scope every traces, metrics, and logs query. Defaults to production.

display.name: LLM calls
display.description: Total model generations (mastra.span.type = model_generation).

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND mastra.span.type = 'model_generation' AND casper.self_instrumented = true

display.name: Total tokens
display.description: Sum of input + output tokens across all model generations.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND mastra.span.type = 'model_generation' AND casper.self_instrumented = true

display.name: Est. cost (USD)
display.description: Derived cost = input_tokens * PRICE_IN + output_tokens * PRICE_OUT, at the real Fireworks kimi-k2p7-code rates ($0.95 / 1M input = 0.00000095, $4.00 / 1M output = 0.000004). This is a trace-side ESTIMATE: it prices the whole input total at the input rate and does not discount cache-read tokens, so it overstates spend on cache-heavy turns. NOTE: with cache pricing unset, the metric counter (gen_ai.client.operation.cost) currently computes the SAME figure — verified equal at $1.0456 over 24h — so neither number is cache-accurate yet. Set LLM_PRICE_CACHE_READ_PER_MTOK / LLM_PRICE_CACHE_WRITE_PER_MTOK and the metric panel becomes the exact cache-split cost while this one stays the upper bound.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND mastra.span.type = 'model_generation' AND casper.self_instrumented = true

display.description: Tool executions grouped by gen_ai.tool.name.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND mastra.span.type = 'tool_call' AND casper.self_instrumented = true

display.name: Errors by type
display.description: Spans carrying error.type (agent/tool/LLM failures), grouped.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND error.type EXISTS

display.name: Answer quality (avg completeness)
display.description: Deterministic completeness score of the agent's answers (0..1), zero-LLM. mastra.span.type = eval.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND mastra.span.type = 'eval'

display.name: Answer quality over time
display.description: avg completeness score per interval — the third axis: is the agent's answer quality drifting?

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND mastra.span.type = 'eval'

display.name: Token rate (metric) by type
display.description: gen_ai.client.token.usage counter, rate/s, grouped by gen_ai.token.type. First-class OTel metric (not a trace attribute).

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment

display.name: LLM cost (metric) by model
display.description: gen_ai.client.operation.cost counter (USD), increase, grouped by model. Native metric — enables PromQL/metric alerts on spend.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment

display.name: Operation p95 latency (metric histogram)
display.description: p95 of the gen_ai.client.operation.duration histogram, grouped by gen_ai.operation.name (chat / execute_tool / retrieve). SigNoz stores an explicit-bucket histogram as separate .bucket/.sum/.count series, so the queryable series is gen_ai.client.operation.duration.bucket and the percentile is taken via spaceAggregation — querying the bare base name returns no data.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment

display.name: RAG retrieval p95 latency
display.description: p95 of the pgvector semantic-recall hop (mastra.span.type = retrieval). The retrieval hop runs on every agent turn — when it degrades, the whole turn slows down before the model is even called.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND mastra.span.type = 'retrieval'

display.name: RAG top similarity score
display.description: Average best-match score returned by the vector search (0..1). A sustained drop means the agent is grounding its answers on progressively worse context — the leading indicator of quality regressions.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND mastra.span.type = 'retrieval'

display.name: Empty retrievals
display.description: Retrieval hops that came back with zero rows — the agent answered with no grounding context at all.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND mastra.span.type = 'retrieval' AND gen_ai.retrieval.returned_count = 0

display.name: Health-watch failures
display.description: Failed runs of the autonomous health-watch cron (mastra.span.type = health_watch). This is the watchdog's own vital sign: if the self-observing loop breaks, every other panel here goes quiet for the wrong reason.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND mastra.span.type = 'health_watch'

display.name: Error logs over time by operation
display.description: The LOGS signal (fifth pillar): correlated ERROR log records the app emits at each failure, count over time grouped by gen_ai.operation.name (chat / execute_tool / retrieve). Every one of these logs carries the failing span's traceId+spanId, so in the Logs explorer you click a line and jump straight to the trace — cross-signal correlation, not just 'logs also exist'. Filter gen_ai.operation.name EXISTS isolates our correlated logs from Mastra's internal log noise.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND gen_ai.operation.name EXISTS

display.name: Error logs by type
display.description: Same correlated ERROR log records, grouped by error.type (bounded label set). Complements the trace 'Errors by type' panel with a first-class LOG view of the same failures — each log line deep-links to its span. This is the panel that makes the Logs signal a first-class citizen of the dashboard instead of an empty tab.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND gen_ai.operation.name EXISTS

display.name: Pipeline: runs
display.description: Distinct agent runs started in the window (count_distinct trace by gen_ai.operation.name = invoke_agent). The top of the pipeline.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND gen_ai.operation.name = 'invoke_agent'

display.name: Pipeline: reached tool
display.description: Distinct runs that executed at least one tool (gen_ai.operation.name = execute_tool — ANY tool, not one hardcoded). Robust to tool renames.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND gen_ai.operation.name = 'execute_tool' AND casper.in_agent_run = true

display.name: Pipeline: reached generation
display.description: Distinct runs that reached a final model generation (our deduped chat span: gen_ai.operation.name = chat AND casper.self_instrumented = true).

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND gen_ai.operation.name = 'chat' AND casper.self_instrumented = true AND casper.in_agent_run = true

display.name: Tool conversion %
display.description: Of the runs that started, what % reached a tool call = reached-tool / runs. Robust attribute-based funnel step 1 -> 2.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND gen_ai.operation.name = 'invoke_agent'
service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND gen_ai.operation.name = 'execute_tool' AND casper.in_agent_run = true

display.name: Generation conversion %
display.description: Of the runs that reached a tool, what % reached a final generation = reached-generation / reached-tool. Funnel step 2 -> 3; a low value means runs error or stall after tools.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND gen_ai.operation.name = 'execute_tool' AND casper.in_agent_run = true
service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND gen_ai.operation.name = 'chat' AND casper.self_instrumented = true AND casper.in_agent_run = true

display.name: Pipeline drop-off over time
display.description: Distinct agent runs reaching each phase over time — runs (invoke_agent), reached-tool (execute_tool, any tool), reached-generation (our deduped chat span). Matched on the stable OTel gen_ai.operation.name attribute, not on span display names, so renames don't break it. The gap between the lines is where runs drop off.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND gen_ai.operation.name = 'invoke_agent'
service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND gen_ai.operation.name = 'execute_tool' AND casper.in_agent_run = true
service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND gen_ai.operation.name = 'chat' AND casper.self_instrumented = true AND casper.in_agent_run = true

display.name: Model failovers
display.description: Times createModel() rerouted off the configured primary to the fallback provider because model-health judged it degraded (mastra.span.type = model_failover). Telemetry-driven failover: SigNoz is the runtime input, not just a dashboard. 0 in a healthy window; a nonzero count means the primary's error-rate or p95 crossed threshold and the system protected the turn on its own.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND mastra.span.type = 'model_failover' AND casper.self_instrumented = true

display.name: Failovers by target & trigger
display.description: model_failover spans grouped by the provider we failed over TO (model.failover.to) and the signal that triggered it (model.failover.source: local = this pod's recent error burst, signoz = fleet-wide error-rate/p95 regression read back from SigNoz, forced = demo override). Answers 'when we rerouted, where did traffic go and what saw the problem first'.

filter.expression: service.name = 'casper-assistant' AND deployment.environment.name = $environment AND mastra.span.type = 'model_failover' AND casper.self_instrumented = true
